data.name: Theodosio
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek words theos (God) and eidos (form, appearance). The name Theodosio means 'Given by God'. This name was borne by several early Christian saints, including Theodosio of Rome and Theodosio of Jerusalem.

in_hebrew.name: תיאודוסיו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם תיאודוסיו מורכב מהמילים היווניות 'תיאוס' ו-'דוסיו', שפירושן אלוהים נתן או שמעאלוהים. השם נמצא בשימוש נוצרי מוקדם ומשקף את האמונה באלוהים כנותן מתנות והשומע תפילות.

in_greek.name: Θεοδόσιος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Θεοδόσιος είναι σύνθετο όνομα από τις λέξεις 'Θεός' (Θεός) και 'δωσις' ή 'ακούω', που σημαίνει 'ο Θεός δίνει' ή 'ακούω τον Θεό'. Το όνομα Θεοδόσιος ήταν κοινό στην αρχαία Εκκλησία και αντανακλά την πίστη στον Θεό ως δωρητή και ακροατή των προσευχών.

in_latin.name: Theodosio
in_latin.long_meaning: Theodosio nomen ex vocibus Graecis 'theos' et 'dosis' vel 'audio' formatum est, quod 'Deus dat' vel 'audi Deus' significat. Nomen hoc in Ecclesia primitiva usu receptum est et fidem in Deum ut datorem et auditorem orationum reflectit.

in_english.name: Theodosio
in_english.meaning: God-given, gift of God, or listener to God
in_english.long_meaning: Theodosio is derived from the Greek words 'theos' (θεός), meaning 'God', and 'dosis' (δωσις) or 'audio', signifying 'given by God' or 'listener to God'. This name was adopted in early Christian tradition, symbolizing faith in God as the giver of gifts and the listener of prayers. Historically, it reflects the spiritual significance of divine providence and communication with God.

saint_reference.note: St. Theodosios the Cenobite, a 5th-century Christian saint and ascetic.

data.cultural_impact: The name Theodosio gained popularity among early Christians not only due to its beautiful meaning but also due to the historical significance of several saints who held this name. Saint Theodosio of Rome, who was pope from 417 to 422 AD, was a crucial figure during the decline of the Western Roman Empire. He helped to restore integrity within the Church and strengthened the role of the papacy. This impact of the name Theodosio is linked to its association with strong and influential Christian leaders.
data.spiritual_significance: Having a name that signifies being "Given by God" is a powerful reminder of the spiritual journey of one's life. The name Theodosio instills a sense of divine guidance, trust, and humility, serving as a constant reminder that every individual's existence and purpose stem from the divine will of God. This spiritual significance adds depth and meaning to the bearing of this name, fostering a connection to God and inspiring a life filled with faith.

historical_references.reference: Theodosius I, also known as Theodosius the Great, was a Roman Emperor from 378 to 395 AD. He was the last emperor to rule over both the Eastern and Western Roman Empires, and is known for issuing the Edict of Thessalonica, which made Christianity the official religion of the Roman Empire.

Theodosius II was the Roman Emperor from 408 to 450 AD. He is known for his significant contributions to the art and architecture of Constantinople, and for his role in the Council of Ephesus, which confirmed the orthodoxy of the Nicene Creed and condemned Nestorianism.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Theodosio has its roots in the Byzantine Empire, a significant period in world history characterized by the political and cultural influence of the Eastern Roman Empire and the spread of Christianity. This name is of particular interest in modern contexts related to history, religion, and classical architecture. On history websites, Theodosio is often discussed in relation to key figures such as Theodosius I, the last Roman emperor to rule the Western Roman Empire and the first Christian Roman emperor, and Theodosius II, the last emperor of the Roman Empire to rule both the Eastern and Western Roman Empires. On religious sites, the name Theodosio is associated with the spread of Christianity during the Byzantine era and the various religious movements and practices that emerged during this time. Lastly, on architecture blogs, the name Theodosio is linked to the classical architectural styles prevalent during the Byzantine Empire, such as the Ravenna Mosaic style, which is still influential in modern architecture.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Theodosio: God's gift of divine law. A name symbolizing the blessings of divine guidance and wisdom in ruling and making just decisions.
